clue.text: Charm sweetheart briefly during date

indicators.note: during means one piece sits within the span of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: to date someone is to see them, as in 'are you seeing anyone?'

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: duck is a northern English term of endearment, like sweetheart

explanation.surface: Advice on winning someone over: whisper a quick term of endearment while out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the last letter and 'during' signals insertion. Duck is a northern English endearment, like 'love'; to date someone is to be seeing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for winning someone over by attraction, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Item of clothing accordingly getting designer label

parts.note: so means therefore, accordingly
CK is the Calvin Klein fashion label

explanation.surface: A garment that, as you'd expect, carries a designer label.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment worn on the foot, so it is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Having no love makes couple give up hope

indicators.note: having no means the next piece is removed from the word

parts.note: does means makes, as in 'does a cake'
O is love, a zero score in tennis
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A lovelorn couple losing all hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having no' takes O out of DOES, leaving DES. Love as zero in tennis gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to lose all expectation, so it matches giving up hope.

clue.text: Questions to do before exams

indicators.note: before puts the swindle word ahead of the exams word

parts.note: to do someone is to con them
tests are exams

explanation.surface: A student's list of queries to work through before exam time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do' is slang for swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs meaning to challenge or dispute something, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: They might mix in resort with short greeting on return

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: on return means the word is read backwards, coming back the way it went
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a salute is a greeting, especially a military one

explanation.surface: A holiday picture: someone at a resort being briefly greeted as they come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the greeting's last letter and 'on return' reverses what remains; 'in' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat kitchen utensils used for stirring and blending ingredients, so they are things that mix.

clue.text: Stop and help crazy pair of Yanks outside

indicators.note: outside means the two-word piece wraps around the other

parts.note: two words for a yank: pull and tug

indicators.note: crazy means the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cry for two Americans to quit acting crazy and help out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yanks' suggests Americans, but it means tugs: two words for a yank, joined, are split open by the 'crazy' rearrangement of help, which sits 'outside' them.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for ending something abruptly, as with switching off a machine at the socket.

clue.text: Watches money invested in banks

indicators.note: invested in places a piece inside another, as money is put into something

parts.note: tiers are banks, rows set one above another

explanation.surface: A financial report about cash being invested with banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests finance, but it means rows of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices that keep time, such as stopwatches; a watch is a timepiece.

clue.text: Connecting line doing tattoo

parts.note: a tattooist is inking skin

explanation.surface: A tattooist drawing a joining line on someone's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining one thing to another, a synonym in the present participle.

clue.text: Deficit quick to come down

parts.note: short means brief, quick
to fall is to come down

explanation.surface: A budget gap that quickly brings someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: An amount by which something falls below what is needed, a synonym for a deficit.

clue.text: Where some might deal cocaine to a crime ring

parts.note: C is slang shorthand for cocaine
a sin is a wrongdoing, loosely a crime
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Describes a drug den where dealers pass cocaine to a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like drug dealing, but it is dealing cards in a gambling house.
explanation.definitionFit: Croupiers deal cards at the tables of a gambling house, so it is a place where some deal.

clue.text: Dance fan second to last in Strictly Come Dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, so these are rearranged
second to last in picks the penultimate letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A viewer of Strictly Come Dancing, the BBC ballroom contest, watching their favourite finish second from bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The TV show's title is broken up: 'Dancing' is the rearrangement signal, acting on fan, one letter of 'Strictly' and 'Come'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery Spanish dance style from Andalusia, so it is one kind of dance.

clue.text: One might create a scene in public, as VIP treatment inept

definitions.text: One might create a scene in public

indicators.note: inept handling garbles things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone making a scene in public because special VIP treatment was handled badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'create a scene' suggests a tantrum, but it means drawing a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Street artists draw chalk pictures on paving stones, literally creating scenes in a public place.

clue.text: Bank on no charge to cough up

parts.note: to bank on something is to expect it
O is nil, nothing
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Expecting a free service, then being made to pay up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cough up' looks like paying money; here it is literal, bringing up phlegm.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up phlegm from the throat or lungs, the literal sense of coughing something up.

clue.text: Bugger! Burst water pipe, right?

indicators.note: a burst pipe breaks apart, so its letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated curse at a burst water pipe, seeking agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bugger!' reads as an oath; it is someone who plants bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugger here is one who plants listening devices, which is what someone tapping phone lines does.

clue.text: Old comedian to attempt joke

parts.note: Ernie Wise, of Morecambe and Wise, the classic British double act
to have a crack is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: A veteran comic trying out a gag.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British comedy duo of the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: A witty remark or quip, so it is a synonym of a joke.

clue.text: Indian place put starter of rice in oven

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of cast-iron range cooker

indicators.note: starter of means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: put the rice in the oven to start the Indian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy British range cooker; R goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Uttar Pradesh, home of the Taj Mahal, so it is an Indian place.

clue.text: Get on grass, let me see plant

parts.note: to get on is to age, grow older
to grass is to inform, to rat on someone
um is a hesitation, a pause while thinking

explanation.surface: Someone muttering while they get on with planting out the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' suggests lawns but is the slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-growing garden flower with fluffy blue heads, so it is a kind of plant.

clue.text: Forward's head to score goal

indicators.note: head to means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A football striker's task: get the head to the ball and score a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' reads as a footballer, but it is the verb, to forward a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a parcel or message is to dispatch it on, a synonym.

clue.text: One turning up on time wearing model's clothes revealing figure

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: 'un is a colloquial form of one, as in 'a good 'un'

indicators.note: wearing means one piece is clothed by the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: the clothes of a word are its outer letters, here M and L of the word model
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A catwalk scene: a model's outfit showing off her figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses in a down clue; 'wearing' puts the period inside the model's outer letters. 'figure' means a digit, not a body.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol for a number, such as 7 or VII, which is a figure.

clue.text: Company after energy that's natural and non-polluting

indicators.note: after places the company abbreviation following the energy symbol

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
a natural conclusion is a logical one

explanation.surface: A firm pursuing energy that is natural and clean, like a green power supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes things kind to the environment, the everyday green sense of the word.

clue.text: White sign over bouncer

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the signal word above the next piece

parts.note: a cue is a sign or signal
a ball bounces

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman in white, displaying a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' suggests a doorman but is anything that bounces. In snooker the white ball is the one the player strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker and pool the white is the ball struck by the cue, so it is named by its colour.

clue.text: River running through Germany twice flooded

indicators.note: running through means one piece flows within the other
twice means the letter appears two times

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A river flowing through Germany burst its banks two times.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England (several share the name).
explanation.definitionFit: Drenched or soaked with water, so the past participle matches flooded.

clue.text: Kinky man, Roger, with condom that's standard

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky sex-comedy scene: a kinky man named Roger with a condom, deemed quite ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means ordinary or run-of-the-mill, so it is a synonym of standard.

clue.text: Bowled OK, conceding runs

definitions.note: the answer is plural, matching the plural runs

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
yes means OK, agreement

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler doing all right but still giving away runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes are runs scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched and the wicketkeeper misses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket extras scored without the bat touching the ball, a specific kind of runs.

clue.text: One found in hanging basket, a rose sprayed with cheap stuff

indicators.note: sprayed scatters the letters about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: tat is cheap, tasteless goods

explanation.surface: A gardening picture: a rose in a hanging basket, sprayed with cheap chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprayed' rearranges ROSE to EROS. The 'hanging basket' is not for flowers but slung beneath a balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter-than-air craft such as a balloon carries its passengers in a basket hanging below it.

clue.text: Sexy old girlfriend going for outfit that's blue

indicators.note: going for means one piece is replaced by another in the word

parts.note: taken as written
an ex is a former partner
a team is an outfit, a group working together

explanation.surface: A racy tale: an old flame changes into an outfit that's sexy and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going for' swaps EX out of SEXY and puts TEAM in. 'Sexy' looks like the definition but is the word being altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue films and steamy scenes are both risqué or erotic, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: What poacher might do to get American bird

definitions.meaning: a poacher might illegally slay a stag on an estate
a North American plover named for its shrill call

explanation.surface: Asks what a poacher would do to bag a bird from America.
explanation.definitionFit: A plover of the Americas, so it is an American bird; read as two words it is a poacher's act.

clue.text: Underwear stores empty around shopping centre

indicators.note: around means the outer letters surround the other piece
empty means the word loses its inside letters, leaving only its ends

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Shops selling underwear sit empty around a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves S and S from 'stores', placed around MALL. 'Smalls' is British slang for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal word for underclothes, especially when laundered.
